correctness.rationale: For the repaired claim, path averaging of molecules gives the edge polytope, whose polar vertices correspond to connected spanning tight-edge graphs. In a bipartite graph, a tight path between endpoints of any cube edge has odd length, so the integer difference is odd and must be ±1. Conversely all-edge tightness gives full rank on the zero-sum hyperplane. An independently written exact enumeration (python3 /workspace/branches/independent_checks.py 4) ranges over even-class heights bounded by distance from the root and uses intersections to extend independently at odd vertices. It obtains 990 potentials and recovers all sixteen representative words, sizes, ranges and centered squared norms by orbit traversal with coordinate swaps, bit flips, and negation. The shell pairs (S, count) are (4,2), (23/4,32), (7,112), (31/4,224), (8,204), (39/4,192), (11,128), (47/4,32), (12,48), (16,16). A normalized support equation gives plane distance S^(-1/2), not necessarily distance to the bounded face. The radial heights (2,3,2,1,0) have S=47/4 and force every point of the exposed face to have coordinate at vertex 0 at most zero, but the orthogonal projection has coordinate 1/94. The repair correctly proves and illustrates this distinction. Repaired scope is the standard Euclidean structure on the coordinate zero-sum space and the specified signed graph group, not arbitrary Euclidean identifications or all abstract symmetries.

value.rationale: This is a complete classification of the canonical Hamming four-cube transportation ball under its natural action, not a selected list of facets. A user studying symmetric transport polytopes can now identify every orbit from explicit representatives and know how many facets support at each radial offset, data unavailable from the raw facet total and centered inball radius. The repaired separation of affine distances from true distances to faces keeps the geometric interpretation precise.
